items.text: Religion and public authority should be kept strictly separate.
items.note: Public authority: the bodies that make and enforce rules for everyone, such as law-makers, courts and officials.
items.rationale: Core separationist item (was rel-04); retagged institutions per review. Mirror of rel-02. Strong frame-splitter.

items.text: A society should have an official religion.
items.note: Official religion: a religion formally recognised and given a special place by public institutions.
items.rationale: Was rel-10; double-barrel removed per review. Establishment supporters agree, separationists disagree. Mirror of rel-01.

items.text: If a society is deeply divided over religion, its laws should be neutral between all religions and none.
items.rationale: Replaces rel-07 (audit unclear: exemptions/lib loading) and rel-05 (near-consensus). Pluralism condition favours Secular. Mirror of rel-04.

items.text: If most people in a society share a religion, its laws should draw on that religion's moral teachings.
items.rationale: Was rel-12 ('reflect' -> 'draw on' per review). Majority condition favours Religious. Mild dem/mul cross-load disclosed.

items.text: Laws should be based on secular reasons alone.
items.note: Secular reasons: reasons that do not depend on any religion's teachings or authority.
items.rationale: Rewrite of rel-01: drops consensus-prone 'reasons any religion can accept'; explicit exclusion of religious grounds. Level 3.

items.text: Religious leaders should have a formal role in making law.
items.note: Formal role: for example, reserved seats in a law-making body or a right to review laws.
items.rationale: Was rel-09 (spec example). Audit pos 1.0. Watch rel x dem correlation in calibration.

items.text: If a society's people follow many different religions or none, its official ceremonies should be free of religious content.
items.rationale: Was rel-06 ('public' -> 'official' per review). Pluralism condition favours Secular. Mirror of rel-08.

items.text: If most people in a society share a religion, its official ceremonies should include that religion's prayers.
items.rationale: New; replaces rel-13 (pro-loaded moral-decline premise) and rel-14 (audit unclear, lib/mul loading). Majority condition favours Religious.

items.text: Public schools open to all children should be free of official prayer and worship.
items.note: Official prayer and worship: led or organised by the school, not pupils praying privately.
items.rationale: Rewrite of rel-02: excludes funded faith schools and private pupil prayer (lib) per review. Mirror of rel-10.

items.text: Public schools open to all children should hold regular official prayer or worship.
items.note: Official prayer or worship: led or organised by the school, not pupils praying privately.
items.rationale: New Religious mirror of rel-09 so school content appears on both poles, per review. Replaces rel-08/rel-11 (rel-11 audit unclear, col loading).

items.text: Laws should rest on reasons anyone can examine and dispute, not on religious authority.
items.rationale: I2 (criticisable law): the Secular pole; adds open criticism to rel-05's secular reasons. Mirrors rel-12. Wording approved by Max Kaye (project owner) for content v2, 2026-10-31; original.

items.text: Some laws should rest on religious revelation and be closed to change by any vote or court.
items.rationale: Revealed, unrevisable law: the Religious pole and the direct opposite of criticisable institutions. Mirrors rel-11. Content v2 separator (CF review 2026-10-31 §5 draft, reworded); original.
